subject: Outbound perimeter & allowlist: justification, ops tasks, and approval request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>, infra-ops@acmehealth.com
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound perimeter & allowlist: justification, ops tasks, and approval request

Hi Liam / Acme infra team —

Thanks again for the time today. As we prepare the Private deployment runbook for Acme's VPC, we need a narrow and auditable outbound allowlist and a short justification bundle so your security team can sign off. Attached is a starting list of candidate egress IPs and a diagram of the control/data-plane flows.

High-level ask: please confirm which of the following you can accept, or provide an alternative approach (proxy/mTLS / customer NAT):

- Static egress IPs for control plane and inference workers (see attached egress-ip-list.csv).
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to those IPs and to S3-like object storage endpoints used for model shards.
- Allow outbound DNS resolution (we recommend DoT/DoH to a customer-managed resolver).
- Block outbound HTTP (port 80) from runtime nodes except for health-checks to internal proxies.

Details we need from your team:
- Are you able to provide static, dedicated NAT IP(s) for our nodes? If not, would you accept a customer-managed outbound proxy (CONNECT/TLS) with client certs?
- Do you require SNI or header-based allowlisting rather than IP-level?
- Any constraints around TLS versions (min TLS 1.2/1.3) or cipher suites?
- Required logging retention and syslog/flowlog endpoints for audit ingestion.

Operational notes from our side:
- Redwood runtime will initiate outbound connections for: control plane heartbeats (control.redwood.ai:443), telemetry (metrics.redwood.ai:443), artifact pulls from object storage, and occasional licensing checks.
- We can configure all traffic to egress via a single outbound proxy if you provide one with a reachable hostname and optionally an mTLS client cert.

Requested next steps: please review the attached CSV and diagram and respond with preferred approach by EOD Monday (7/19). If you want, we can schedule a 30-min ops run-through.

Thanks —
Marcus
VP, Customer Deployment
Redwood Inference
(attachment: egress-ip-list.csv, firewall-diagram.png)

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Outbound perimeter & allowlist: justification, ops tasks, and approval request

Thanks Marcus — quick answers inline.

On Wed, Jul 15, 2026 at 09:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> High-level ask: please confirm which of the following you can accept...

We run in a managed VPC with NAT gateway clusters and can provide a small set of static egress IPs for approved workloads. We need the following clarified before we sign off:

1) Will Redwood runtime nodes open persistent outbound connections or only short-lived HTTPS calls? Our security team prefers short-lived, client-initiated connections to known hosts.
2) Do you require outbound access to arbitrary S3 endpoints (i.e., third-party buckets), or only to vendor-hosted model stores? We need a list of hostnames/IPs.
3) We have an existing customer-managed proxy that supports TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS. Can Redwood present a client cert to that proxy?
4) Our compliance team requires flow logs for the nodes and 365-day retention on any firewall logs associated with external egress.

We can accept: static egress IPs, outbound port 443 only, and DNS over TLS to our resolver (resolver.acmeinternal:853). We do not allow DNS to public resolvers.

I'll have InfraOps send our NAT IP ranges and proxy details once we confirm the host list.

—Liam
Infrastructure Manager, Acme Health

(Quoted above for context)

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Outbound perimeter & allowlist: justification, ops tasks, and approval request

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick follow-up and for confirming the DoT resolver and static NATs. To answer your questions in more detail:

1) Connection patterns: runtime nodes primarily make short-lived outbound TLS connections for: artifact pulls (model shards), control heartbeats, telemetry batching, and license checks. There is no requirement for inbound from Redwood to your network. We do keep long-lived TLS sessions in some high-throughput paths (session reuse) but those are client-initiated.

2) Host list: attached CSV contains canonical hostnames we use (control.redwood.ai, artifacts.redwood-storage.s3.amazonaws.com, metrics.redwood.ai) plus a small set of CDN/registry addresses. If you prefer hostname allowlisting, we can provide a signed list of hostnames and ASN ranges, but most enterprises require IP-level allowlist for edge NATs.

3) Proxy & mTLS: Redwood private runtime supports egress via customer-managed HTTP CONNECT proxy. We can present a client cert and will also support strict SNI verification if required. To operate via your proxy we need: proxy hostname, port, and CA chain to validate the proxy if it terminates TLS to our nodes. If you require mutual TLS between runtime and proxy, we can coordinate cert exchange (we prefer a short-lived cert with rotation).

4) Logging & retention: we will enable VPC flow logs for the runtime subnets and forward them to your provided syslog/S3 endpoint. By default we keep internal metrics for 30 days; for audit logs we can retain delivery to your SIEM indefinitely if you ingest the flowlogs.

Firewall rule recommendation (minimal):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from runtime subnets to the egress IP set (attached).
- Allow outbound TCP 853 from runtime subnets to resolver.acmeinternal (DoT).
- Deny outbound TCP 80 from runtime subnets to internet.
- Allow outbound DNS only to your resolver (deny 53/udp to public resolvers).

Operational caveats:
- If your NAT IPs rotate (e.g., per AZ), we need a stable set for the duration of the rollout; otherwise we recommend using the customer proxy approach.
- If you prefer hostname-based allowlist, please provide the upstream firewall product and version so we can validate SNI passthrough behavior.

Happy to hop on a call to finalize.

—Camila
Product Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

(attachment: updated-egress-hosts.csv)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Outbound perimeter & allowlist: justification, ops tasks, and approval request

Hi all — adding the compliance checklist from our side so procurement/security at Acme have clarity:

- TLS policy: enforce TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers. For mTLS flows, require mutual authentication and cert rotation every 90 days.
- Auditability: enable flow logs, and provide a delivery endpoint (S3 or SIEM) with 365-day retention for any logs associated with this integration.
- Data exfil risk: runtime nodes must not be allowed outbound to arbitrary IP ranges—restrict to the provided egress set and to your resolver.
- SBOM/Dependency disclosures: provide the control-plane hostname and a short statement that no PII is transmitted in telemetry payloads; instrumentation payloads are metrics-only unless customer opts-in to additional logs.
- Change control: any change to allowlisted IPs or proxy configuration must be communicated 5 business days ahead and follow your change advisory board process.

If Acme can confirm the NAT IPs and/or proxy details and accept the 5-business-day change window, Compliance can sign off on the firewall policy.

—Olga
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — short summary and action items:

Agreed approach:
- Acme will provide a small set of static NAT IPs for the Redwood runtime to egress from (InfraOps to send list).
- DoT resolver (resolver.acmeinternal:853) will be used for DNS; no public resolvers allowed.
- Outbound allowed: TCP 443 to the egress IPs + approved object storage hostnames; TCP 853 to resolver. Block TCP 80.
- Redwood will support customer-managed proxy with mTLS as an alternative if NATs cannot be allocated.
- Compliance: flow logs enabled + 365d retention; TLS 1.2+; 90-day client cert rotation for mTLS flows.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- InfraOps (Acme) — share static NAT IP ranges and proxy details (if using) by Tue 7/20.
- Camila — finalize the canonical host/IP list and produce a signed hostlist artifact (Confluence) by Wed 7/21.
- Olga — prepare the compliance signoff template and 5-business-day change-policy language by Wed 7/21.
- Marcus — schedule 30-min ops run-through once NAT IPs/proxy details are received.

I'll attach the current CSV and diagram here for your record and push a final runbook to the Confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/NET/Private+Deployment+Egress+Playbook

If there are no objections, I'll treat this as the working plan and proceed with the rollout checklist.

—Marcus
